entries.title: Invention Conceptualization
entries.summary: The design-brief stage that defines function, user, operating conditions, complexity, skills, materials, and limits.
body: Invention Conceptualization is one stage of [[invention-system|Kaysender’s converted invention procedure]]. It turns the source workflow into a repeatable Hypertext d20-compatible downtime process.
This stage should create records the group can use later: a design brief, research notes, material ledger, work-unit log, test record, flaw list, or improvement history.

sections.heading: Converted procedure
body: Write a one-paragraph design brief stating exactly what the invention does, who or what uses it, its intended operating environment, and the problem it solves.
Select a complexity from Routine, Standard, Complex, Advanced, or Revolutionary. Record the project DC and required work units from [[invention-system|the invention system]].
Choose one primary construction skill, one testing skill, the required facility, the expected market price, the raw-material budget, and every magical, legal, or rare-component prerequisite.

Define one explicit limitation. Examples include limited charges, required fuel, setup time, maintenance, size, fixed installation, environmental vulnerability, or a check required for difficult operation.
GM approval at this stage confirms only that the project may be attempted. It does not guarantee access to components, uninterrupted work, legal certification, or a successful result.

sections.heading: Project record
body: Record the responsible character, assistants, date, location, facility, check result, modifiers, time spent, materials spent or lost, progress completed, and any new flaw or obligation.
Where a source table used overlapping thresholds, this conversion uses ordinary d20 checks: meet or exceed the DC for success; margins of 5 and 10 determine exceptional results or severe failure.

entries.title: Invention Research and Development
entries.summary: The converted research procedure for establishing a viable design path before committing resources.
body: Invention Research and Development is one stage of [[invention-system|Kaysender’s converted invention procedure]]. It turns the source workflow into a repeatable Hypertext d20-compatible downtime process.
This stage should create records the group can use later: a design brief, research notes, material ledger, work-unit log, test record, flaw list, or improvement history.

sections.heading: Converted procedure
body: Spend at least one day consulting references, experts, prior devices, experiments, or magical theory.
Attempt a relevant Knowledge, Spellcraft, Profession, or Craft check against the project DC. Success grants +2 on the first construction check; exceeding the DC by 5 grants +4 instead.

Failure by 4 or less produces useful notes but no modifier. Failure by 5 or more reveals a false assumption and imposes -2 on construction until the inventor spends another day revising the design and repeats the research check.
A different researcher may repeat the check only by contributing a genuinely different source, method, or field of expertise. Repeated identical rolls do not represent new research.
Research can reveal a required component, permit, or specialist that was not obvious during conceptualization.

entries.title: Invention Materials and Preparation
entries.summary: The converted procurement and material-quality procedure for tying components to an invention’s purpose.
body: Invention Materials and Preparation is one stage of [[invention-system|Kaysender’s converted invention procedure]]. It turns the source workflow into a repeatable Hypertext d20-compatible downtime process.
This stage should create records the group can use later: a design brief, research notes, material ledger, work-unit log, test record, flaw list, or improvement history.

sections.heading: Converted procedure
body: Raw materials normally cost one-third of expected market price. The project cannot begin until the listed facility, tools, common materials, and rare components are available.

Improvised or reclaimed materials cost 75 percent of the normal raw-material budget and impose -2 on construction and testing. Fine materials cost 150 percent and grant +2. Exceptional materials cost 300 percent and grant +4.

Appraise evaluates quality and authenticity. Gather Information or Profession locates suppliers. Survival finds natural components. Knowledge identifies appropriate magical, biological, geological, or engineering materials.
A successful procurement check locates a credible source; it does not automatically purchase, steal, transport, refine, or legally clear the material.
Substitution is possible only when the design brief is revised. A substitute may alter damage type, weight, capacity, maintenance, environmental tolerance, or another operating characteristic.

entries.title: Invention Crafting and Enchanting
entries.summary: The converted work-unit procedure for manufacturing, assembling, or enchanting the approved design.
body: Invention Crafting and Enchanting is one stage of [[invention-system|Kaysender’s converted invention procedure]]. It turns the source workflow into a repeatable Hypertext d20-compatible downtime process.
This stage should create records the group can use later: a design brief, research notes, material ledger, work-unit log, test record, flaw list, or improvement history.

sections.heading: Converted procedure
body: Each qualified primary crafter can attempt one construction check after eight hours of productive work. Success completes 1 work unit, plus 1 additional unit for every 5 points by which the check exceeds the project DC.

Failure by 1–4 completes no work and wastes 10 percent of the remaining raw-material budget. Failure by 5–9 also adds a minor flaw. Failure by 10 or more causes a major accident and destroys at least 25 percent of remaining materials.
Up to three qualified assistants may use aid another during the same work period. Assistants cannot simultaneously advance separate projects.

Enchanting additionally requires the relevant spell access, caster level, item-creation feat, ritual, or setting equivalent. The Craft or Spellcraft check measures execution; it does not replace magical prerequisites.
Interruptions, unsafe movement, hostile weather, damaged workshops, exhausted workers, and missing utilities can suspend work or impose circumstance penalties.

entries.title: Invention Testing and Certification
entries.summary: The converted field-testing procedure for exposing flaws before an invention is trusted, sold, or installed.
body: Invention Testing and Certification is one stage of [[invention-system|Kaysender’s converted invention procedure]]. It turns the source workflow into a repeatable Hypertext d20-compatible downtime process.
This stage should create records the group can use later: a design brief, research notes, material ledger, work-unit log, test record, flaw list, or improvement history.

sections.heading: Converted procedure
body: Testing begins after every required work unit is complete. Spend at least one hour operating, casting, firing, loading, flying, or installing the invention under realistic conditions.

Attempt the designated testing skill against the project DC. Success validates normal operation. Exceeding the DC by 5 identifies one free minor optimization, such as clearer controls, easier access, or a maintenance note granting +2 on the next repair check.
Failure reveals a flaw selected by the GM or generated from the flaw guidance in [[invention-system|the invention system]]. Failure by 5 or more triggers the flaw during the test.
A failed test does not always destroy the project. The flaw can be accepted and documented, repaired through an improvement project, or concealed at legal and reputational risk.

Certification is a separate social and regulatory step. A guild inspector, captain, government office, insurer, temple, or military command may demand plans, test records, fees, or an independent demonstration.

entries.title: Invention Improvement
entries.summary: The converted iteration procedure for strengthening a working design without unlimited bonus stacking.
body: Invention Improvement is one stage of [[invention-system|Kaysender’s converted invention procedure]]. It turns the source workflow into a repeatable Hypertext d20-compatible downtime process.
This stage should create records the group can use later: a design brief, research notes, material ledger, work-unit log, test record, flaw list, or improvement history.

sections.heading: Converted procedure
body: An improvement uses the original project DC +5, costs 25 percent of the item’s market price, and requires one-quarter of the original work units, rounded up.
Success adds one bounded improvement: +1 on one narrow use, 25 percent greater capacity or range, 25 percent less fuel or maintenance, one extra daily use, faster setup, or removal of one flaw.

Failure by 1–4 consumes time and 10 percent of the improvement budget. Failure by 5–9 temporarily disables the item until repaired. Failure by 10 or more damages the original invention and creates a major flaw.
An invention may hold no more than three improvements. Further development requires a rebuild as a project of the next higher complexity.
An improvement cannot bypass a class prerequisite, magical prerequisite, creature immunity, or the normal enhancement limits of the ruleset.

entries.title: Invention Success Factors and Failure Costs
entries.summary: The converted circumstance-modifier and consequence guidance for ambitious projects.
body: Invention Success Factors and Failure Costs is one stage of [[invention-system|Kaysender’s converted invention procedure]]. It turns the source workflow into a repeatable Hypertext d20-compatible downtime process.
This stage should create records the group can use later: a design brief, research notes, material ledger, work-unit log, test record, flaw list, or improvement history.

sections.heading: Converted procedure
body: Favorable factors include fine materials, specialized facilities, relevant prior designs, expert assistance, adequate funding, extra research, and controlled operating conditions. Each should normally provide +2, with exceptional materials or a unique master facility providing +4.

Unfavorable factors include improvised materials, damaged tools, inadequate facilities, turbulence, rushed deadlines, secrecy, missing documentation, contaminated components, and unfamiliar magic. Each normally imposes -2; severe conditions may impose -4 or prevent work.
Time pressure should not be represented by unlimited repeat attempts. Halving available work time imposes -4 and turns any failure by 5 or more into a major accident.
Failure costs should be recorded in the project ledger: materials lost, work units lost, flaws introduced, injuries, repairs required, legal exposure, and obligations to patrons or assistants.
After two consecutive failures at the same stage, another attempt requires a changed method, replacement component, additional research, new specialist, or improved facility.
